All costs, times, and task-fit scores in this planner are invented demo estimates—not provider prices, measurements, or guarantees. The planner selects among eligible routes using the chosen preference. It shows the smart-routing product direction; current implementation scope is described in the open chassis.

A model router chooses which model handles a request.
A web router chooses how the agent reaches the web.
The decision can span indexed search, live extraction, a browser, or a deeper research workflow—and then the provider behind that approach.

02 / The field guide

FAMILIAR HARDWARE.
NEW POSSIBILITIES.

We already know what a router does for our devices. That same visual language gives agent infrastructure a shape people can understand.

FIG. 02 / CONNECT

Your agent is
the new device.

A computer connects once to reach the network. An agent connects through a common interface to access web capabilities.

ETHERNET / WI-FI → MCP / LIBRARY

A port for
every capability.

Search, extract, research, and browse each have a clear place. Providers sit behind those capabilities as replaceable adapters.

03 / At the boundary

YOUR NETWORK.
YOUR RULES.

A router gives a network a boundary. WebRouter gives us a familiar way to explain checks on what an agent sends out and what comes back.

HOW AN ADAPTER FITS +

Map the provider's requests and responses to the common interface, declare its supported capabilities, and test the integration. Each new adapter adds another option for the router.

This directory shows the WebRouter provider ecosystem. Capabilities and availability depend on the adapter, account, and deployment; managed access may differ. Browse includes browser sessions and browser-agent tools.
